label: gasaigo
title: 〜が最後
meaning: If s.o. does s.t for even a moment, the following result will necessarily occur • Once someone starts something, the person can’t stop it 〜したら • いったん〜たらそのまま • いったん〜たら必ず
meaning_example: If the boss even touches  the mic for a second, he won't let anyone else sing karaoke ALL night

notes.text:
see http://www.geocities.com/easykanji/jlptgrammar.html



Once someone starts something, the person can’t stop it.



Notes: Easily confused with ~kiri, but the meanings are completely different and ga saigo doesn’t mean ‘for the last time’. Always used with past tense verbs.

食べ出したが最後、おいしくて止められなかった

		The opening sentence is good. "I want you to listen to the following story". 
		If you just 
		obediently lean in your ears, it's certain that you won't be able to stop (reading).  (Nikkei book review)
